mentl/a9a1dc5:
The next build rested on a cause: 52 "no live install: lower_scope"
floors in the frame variant's wheel prove the handler is absent at
lower_state_field_inits. The law added this morning gates acting on an
unverified cause, so the baseline got counted first.

The baseline has 50. The delta is +2, exactly the number of new ls_ call
sites the variant added. The mechanism survives; the evidence as written
did not. An absolute count proves nothing without its baseline, and the
baseline cost one march. Unchecked, this would have been the sixth
refuted cause in this arc and the first to steer a build.

It also sharpens the question, because a second measured fact does not
fit "the handler is not installed": the baseline compiles the nested
repro to a non-empty 38568-byte WAT carrying the MissingName marker for
start, and reaching that marker requires ls_resolve to have returned
RGlobal at this very site. So lower_scope is reachable here at runtime
and the two added sites floored at emit time. Two mechanisms, one
measured, no design resting on either.

The next instrument is the output: is the emit's singleton-install proof
per call site? ls_resolve in lower_expr's shared VarRef arm does not
floor; the added ls_enter_frame does. Per-site keeps the frame route
alive; per-handler kills it and leaves the structural rewrite. One
measurement decides, and nothing is built before it.

mentl/a99cf69:
Three gates each re-derived the identical boot(wheel) compile (~13 min)
into three directories: verify's census, march's m2, march-gate's m2.
The compile is deterministic (the monotonic bump image; every byte-exact
m2 == m3 assert is the empirical proof), so it is a pure function of
(wheel bytes, boot bytes, run flags) — Carried-Truth applied to the
tools: wt_m2_ensure fills ONE keyed artifact under .build/m2cache and
every consumer reads it; a flock serializes concurrent gates.

verify.sh is idempotent now: a green run stamps wt_state_key (wheel +
boot + micros + the gate scripts themselves); a re-run on the unchanged
state — above all the pre-commit hook seconds after a green — answers
from the stamp instead of re-paying the full battery (measured: 34ms vs
~15min). FORCE_VERIFY=1 re-runs; --from-seed never stamps (a different
compiler).

march.sh arbitrates the ratchet itself: on m2 != m3 it runs the m4 leg
and rules TRANSITION (m3 == m4 — an emit/import change crossing one
generation, re-pin from m3) vs BROKEN (m3 != m4). Blessing the wrong
generation was the one human-error surface in the boot era; today's
record-base transition was hand-driven and this closes that class.
Placement into consumer dirs copies, never hardlinks — every tool
overwrites its own output paths, and a hardlink would write back into
the cache inode.
mentl/a9b797e:
mentl2`s lexer scan_string_chunk treated backslash-escape as a chunk
break-byte, flushing a SEPARATE TStringPart per escape:
"a\nb" → TStringPart("a"),TStringPart("\n"),TStringPart("b") (3 parts,
NO TStringSplice). parse_string_interpolation only coalesces parts
across a TStringSplice, so consecutive escape-split parts dangled —
parse_call_args expect(TRParen) hard-failed on the orphan parts. (Body
position tolerated the dangling tokens, masking it: identical tokens
parsed clean as a fn body but failed as a call argument — first
pass-3 wheel divergence at src/backends/wasm.mn:115,
perform wat_emit("...\n").)

Converge wheel → seed (the arbiter; pass-2 proves it). Seed
lex_main.wat:98-112 emits ONE TString with escapes resolved inline via
$str_unescape (SYNTAX.md §1077: \n \r \t \\ \" \0), per
Hβ.first-light.lexer-string-escape-substrate. Wheel fix:

- Add str_unescape (lib/runtime/strings.mn) — two-pass mirror of seed
  bootstrap/src/runtime/str.wat $str_unescape: count decoded length,
  one alloc, byte-store fill. Two-pass IS the O(N²)-bomb avoidance the
  scan_string comment warned of (single alloc, no per-byte concat).
- scan_string_chunk: delete the per-escape-flush branch (it WAS the
  design flaw the parser then had to un-coalesce — Anchor 2: delete,
  don`t decorate). `\X` is now a transparent 2-byte non-break span
  (chunk_start unchanged so `\"` does not falsely close). Resolve
  escapes once via str_unescape at all 5 chunk-flush sites
  (EOF / `"` / `{{` / `}}` / `{`-splice).

Empirical: pass-2 1981 fns (+3 str_unescape*, valid WASM, no
regression). T3 g("a\nb") + S6 perform wat_emit("...\n") parse clean.
pass-3 first divergence advances src/backends/wasm.mn:115 → input 227.
Remaining (distinct, NOT this handle): `{x}` interpolation splice path
S4 `"val={x}"` still fails — #138 parse_string_interpolation splice
loop.
mentl/a9a8ba6:
Attempted FV.1 at max effort. Discovered that `!E` declared on
monomorphic closed rows is algebraically collapsed by
`normalize_inter` in std/compiler/effects.ka:134-156 before
`row_subsumes` sees it. `Closed(A) & !Closed(B)` reduces to
`Closed(A - B)`, which is just `Closed(A)` when B ⊄ A — meaning
explicit `!E` on a closed-row fn whose body doesn't perform E
adds nothing the closed-row-ness didn't already prove.

The compiler is monomorphic at every site investigated 2026-04-22
(infer_program, lower_program, emit_module, cache_write / cache_read,
driver_* functions all carry closed declared rows). Applying FV.1
as originally framed would be decoration, not substrate.

`!E` earns load-bearing weight only on:
- Effect-polymorphic open rows (`EfOpen(pos, v) & !Closed([E])`
  genuinely narrows what v can bind to)
- Row-negation forms at the top level (universe-minus-E semantics)

FV.1 reframed as two peer sub-handles:

- **FV.1.α — substrate decision.** Keep current algebra (`!E` on
  closed rows is a no-op; FV.1 doesn't apply) vs preserve declared
  negation as separate signature metadata accessible to audit /
  Mentl / code-review surfaces. Needs walkthrough before code.

- **FV.1.β — polymorphic effect-row exemplar.** Find a higher-order
  site where the callback's row is genuinely polymorphic and
  declare `!E` as a narrowing constraint. Candidate: prelude.ka's
  higher-order collection ops. Needs walkthrough before code (API
  change risk).

Handoff Posture queue table updated: FV.1 marked BLOCKED.
'Do NOT attempt in Antigravity' section added listing FV.1 and
FV.8 as items that need walkthrough or fresh Claude Code tier.

This is drift-mode-9 refused: the honest move is to name the peer
sub-handles and document the finding, not to commit decorative
`!E` that would read as FV.1 applied but add no substrate.
